video_title: Bobby Marks' OKC Thunder Offseason Guide ⚡️ Who is DESTINED to be traded?! | NBA on ESPN

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC Thunder's unique position under the new CBA rules
quotes.excerpt: I think OKC is in a unique situation just based on where we are with the rules
quotes.quote: I think the Thunder are probably the most anticipated team to keep an eye on this offseason. I think certainly when you look at other teams, of course the Lakers, I think OKC is in a unique situation just based on where we are with the rules of the CBA. People want to know, are they going to be another casualty of the second apron? What is going to happen with their roster?

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC Thunder's draft capital and roster flexibility
quotes.excerpt: 12, 17, and 37. The pick 12 is from the Clippers from the Paul George trade
quotes.quote: 64 and 18, another 61 season. Three picks: 12, 17, and 37. The pick 12 is from the Clippers from the Paul George trade. They and Atlanta are the only two playoff teams that have a lottery pick. The 17th pick is from Philadelphia as part of the Al Horford trade.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC Thunder's financial outlook and second apron status
quotes.excerpt: You are $40 million above the second apron. This is going to be the talking point
quotes.quote: You are $40 million above the second apron. This is going to be the talking point to summer. You are at 261, that includes your 15 players, it includes your two draft picks. You are $40 million above the second apron. Your projected payroll, this does not include your first round picks, you are at 213 and then add another close to 250. So your payroll is the highest in probably projected to be in league history here.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Brad Stevens on Boston's limited trade tools
quotes.excerpt: We've been limited in what tools we can use with where we are right now around
quotes.quote: I pulled a quote from Brad Stevens and it said, we've been limited in what tools we can use with where we are right now around the second apron. The tools that he mentioned basically is the inability to send out cash in a trade, use at least 6.1 of the non-tax mid-level exception, the inability to take back more salary in a trade, the inability to aggregate contracts in a trade.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Why OKC cannot easily trade for high-salary players
quotes.excerpt: You cannot trade a $50 million player for a $58 million because you are taking back more salary
quotes.quote: When you aggregate contracts, you cannot have your post-transaction salary over the second apron. You cannot trade a $50 million player for a $58 million because you are taking back more salary. And even if you wanted to say, we're going to decline Lu Dort and Kenrich Williams and that's $25 million, you are still a first and second apron team. I don't see a scenario where you're not going to be a second apron team.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: The likelihood of Isaiah Hartenstein remaining with OKC
quotes.excerpt: I will bet anybody a dinner or a donation to your charity that Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.quote: I love when people say, well, they're just going to decline Isaiah Hartenstein and he's going to become a free agent. I will bet anybody a dinner or a donation to your charity that Isaiah Hartenstein will be a free agent and playing elsewhere next year. If his option is declined, that means they have an agreement in place that he will be back on probably a longer contract and at less money.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Cason Wallace as an extension candidate
quotes.excerpt: Extension candidate to watch, of course, is Cason Wallace. Oklahoma City has been aggressive with extension talks
quotes.quote: Extension candidate to watch, of course, is Cason Wallace. Oklahoma City has been aggressive with extension talks on all-NBA defender. I am not going to put comps out and put numbers out because that just pisses people off, but I would expect them to be aggressive when it comes to Wallace extension.
